Davanti a una massa surrenalica incident:
When faced with an incidental adrenal mass, size, unenhanced attenuation and post-contrast behavior matter. Unenhanced attenuation ≤ 10 HU = lipid-rich adenoma (no further work-up). Above 10 HU, a washout CT (absolute ≥ 60% or relative ≥ 40% at 15 minutes suggest adenoma) or chemical-shift MRI is needed.
Size over 4 cm, irregular margins, heterogeneity, necrosis, calcifications and growth point toward adrenocortical carcinoma. Hormonal secretion must always be excluded, in particular pheochromocytoma before any invasive procedure: for this reason biopsy is not a first step and, if carcinoma is suspected, it is avoided because of the risk of seeding.
In the report: size, relationship with the liver, kidney and inferior vena cava (tumor thrombus of the cava or adrenal vein), lymph nodes and metastases.
Massa surrenalica > 4 cm, eterogenea, >: Adrenal mass > 4 cm, heterogeneous, > 10 HU unenhanced: think of carcinoma; hormonal tests first, no routine biopsy.
Carcinoma corticosurrenalico, diagnosi i: Adrenocortical carcinoma, histologic diagnosis (Adrenal-ACC-Ki67-Seg collection): pathologic diameter 11.2 cm, stage T3 N0 M0, Ki-67 10%.
La massa surrenalica era già nota (risco: The adrenal mass was already known (incidental finding) and this CT is meant precisely to characterize it: the requesting physician will read the report, which must state the suspicion of carcinoma and the recommended completion (delayed-phase CT or MRI, endocrinologic and surgical evaluation). A documented communication within a few days is nonetheless acceptable.
